headline: The AI money is circling, and the payoff hasn't arrived
summary: This week the question moved from what agents can do to who is paying, and for what. BIS found that 55.2% of investment into AI firms from 2021 to 2025 came from other AI firms, while Apollo sees revenue per worker and margins rising for the Mag 7 but flat for the S&P 493. The buildout is also hitting physical limits: US computer imports have far outpaced production since 2019, and a16z now calls skilled labor a bottleneck. The attack surface keeps growing too, and Sam Altman says we can no longer just patch all the bugs. Builders are answering with less, not more: a study and Anthropic's own guide both find one well-equipped agent often matches or beats elaborate multi-agent setups. For you, that means tying every AI budget to a measured return, funding the simplest agent design that works, and asking whether your vendors' revenue comes from customers or from each other.

threads.title: Less agent, more result
threads.line: One capable agent often beats a team of them. Fund the simplest design that works, then demand proof it works.

threads.title: Bugs outrun patches
threads.line: Altman says patching every bug no longer works. Fund AI-assisted defense and scan every skill your agents install.
